response.rationale: The CT shows a large heterogenous necrotic adrenal mass with contiguous invasion into adjacent organs and regional lymphadenopathy, a pattern characteristic of adrenal cortical carcinoma. R5 lacks a renal primary; R3 has only nonspecific pain and hypertension without catecholamine crisis; R4 has historical B symptoms and lymph nodes but the B symptoms are temporally remote and the locally invasive adrenal mass favors ACC; R6 is contradicted by the destructive mass.

rejected.why: Family history of RCC is nonspecific and no renal primary mass is described; a locally invasive adrenal mass favors a primary adrenal tumor.
Hypertension and flank pain are nonspecific; no paroxysmal catecholamine symptoms and invasive local growth make pheochromocytoma unlikely.
B symptoms and lymphadenopathy are suggestive, but the B symptoms are historical rather than current and the CT shows a single locally invasive adrenal mass more typical of ACC; LDH is normal.
Autoimmune history and azathioprine exposure do not explain a large necrotic adrenal mass with local invasion; adrenalitis is contradicted by the imaging.
